policies.title: Named ordinary passports: no Grenada entry visa
policies.summary: The active Ministry of Foreign Affairs schedule explicitly marks these named ordinary-nationality rows ‘No Visa required’.
conditions: The schedule defines this label as ‘Visa not required for entry’. It gives nationality-specific maximum stays in some rows, so no common duration is inferred.
The schedule says visitors remaining beyond their permitted 14-day, 30-day, 60-day, 90-day or six-month period, or visiting to work, study or reside, must obtain a visa.

The current Embassy page confirms that visa requirements depend on citizenship, not country of residence. It separately confirms a 30-day exemption for a valid PRC passport; non-Chinese PRC permanent residents are not covered by that nationality rule.
The required online Immigration and Customs form opens 72 hours before arrival and is an arrival declaration, not an ETA or visa.

This does not establish diplomatic, official, service, UN laissez-passer, cruise-transit, residence, work, study, crew, refugee, stateless, emergency or other special-document treatment. Admission remains subject to immigration control.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa at Grenada port of entry
policies.summary: The active Ministry of Foreign Affairs schedule explicitly labels these ordinary-nationality rows ‘Port of Entry’, defined as a visa granted on arrival in Grenada.
conditions: The schedule defines ‘Port of Entry’ as ‘Visa granted on arrival in Grenada’. No common duration, fee, purpose, eligible entry point or document checklist is stated for this cohort.
This is distinct from the Embassy’s prior-arrival application process, which requires filing before travel and may result in an emailed visa or issuance at arrival after approval.
The required online Immigration and Customs form opens 72 hours before arrival and is not an ETA or a visa.
Work, study, residence, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, UN laissez-passer, refugee, stateless and other special-document cases are outside this ordinary-passport visitor policy.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance Grenada visa
policies.summary: The active Ministry of Foreign Affairs schedule explicitly labels these ordinary-nationality rows ‘Prior to Arrival’, which it defines as a visa obtained at a Grenada mission or consulate before travel.
conditions: The schedule defines ‘Prior To Arrival’ as a visa obtained at a Grenada mission or consulate before travel. The current Embassy process says applications must be submitted at least six weeks before departure and indicates about ten business days’ processing from receipt.

The current Embassy process says an approved visa may be emailed before arrival or issued at arrival. Because every route requires an advance mission application and approval, this is normalized as visa_required, not evisa or visa_on_arrival.

The Embassy lists a passport valid six months beyond departure, photographs, fee, travel/accommodation evidence and a Grenada host invitation as application requirements; visas do not authorize work without Labour Ministry permission.
The required online Immigration and Customs form opens 72 hours before arrival and is not an ETA or a visa.
The policy does not establish diplomatic, official, service, UN laissez-passer, cruise-transit, residence, work, study, crew, refugee, stateless or other special-document treatment.

application.label: Grenada Embassy prior-arrival visa process
application.processingTime: The Embassy states applications must be submitted at least six weeks before departure and processing is approximately ten business days from receipt.
steps: Confirm the ordinary-passport nationality is a ‘Prior To Arrival’ row in the active Ministry schedule.
Submit the completed application and supporting passport, photograph, travel, accommodation, host-invitation and fee evidence to a Grenada mission or consulate before travel.
Carry the approval and required travel documents; the Embassy says the approved visa may be emailed before arrival or issued at arrival after approval.
